2 Simple Proof

This section presents a simple proof of the Apex Minor Theorem. The next lemma is the key. A centre of a graph G is a vertex a E V(G) such that max{dist (a,v) : v € V(G)} is equal to the radius of G.

Lemma 10. Let A be a planar graph such that A - z is a minor of the k × k grid for some z EV(A). Let G be an A-minor-free graph with radius r and centre a. Then G - a has no k" × k" grid minor.

Proof. We proceed by induction on r. In the r = 0 case, V(G - a) = I and the result holds. Now consider the radius r case, and assume the radius r - 1 case holds. Let Vi := {x E V(G) : distG(x, a) = i} for i € {0, ...,r}. So Vo = {a} and VoU... UV, = V(G). Suppose for the sake of contradiction that G - a has a k" × k' grid minor. Partition this k" × k" grid into k × k subgrids, so that contracting each subgrid to a vertex gives a ー1xだー1 grid. First suppose that some k × k subgrid is contained in Vr. Thus H is a minor of G|Vr]. By construction, G Vo U•. U Vr-1] is connected. Let G' be obtained from G by contracting VoU.. UVr-1 to a vertex w. Since every vertex in Vr has a neighbour in Vr-1, every vertex in G' is at distance at most 1 from w. Since H is a minor of G[V], A is a minor of G and thus of G, which is a contradiction. Now assume that every k × k subgrid intersects VIU... UVr-1. Let G' be obtained from G by contracting each subgrid to a vertex, and deleting any vertices in Vr not in one of the subgrids. So every vertex in G' is at distance at most r - 1 from a, and G' - a contains a k"-1 × k"-1 grid minor. Since G' is a minor of G, G' is A-minor-free. Hence G' contradicts the assumed truth of the r - 1 case.

Therefore, G - a has no k" × k" grid minor.

Lemmas 2 and 10 imply that for every apex graph A with t vertices, every A-minor-free graph G with radius r has no (2t - 2)" × (2t - 2)' grid minor. Equation (1) implies that tw(G) € O* ((2t)9r). This completes our simple proof of the Apex Minor Theorem by Eppstein |18| (Theorem 4).

3 Polynomial Upper Bound

This section proves Theorem 5 from Section 1. We need the following straightforward lemma.

Lemma 11. If a graph G is a minor of the k × I grid, then there is an H-model (Bu : u E V(H)) in the 2k × 2l grid J, such that for each vertex u E V(H) there is a vertex hu in Bu incident to no edge of J representing an edge of H.
